notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.

Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay St. Charles County and, in the counties that have them, the township they live in.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
The city borrowed $21,585,000 during the year, which is not counted as revenue but helps explain spending above revenue.
Debt service leaves out $6,160,000 of principal repaid with new borrowing the city did not spend on capital that year, most likely refinancing or a rolled-over note.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: Missouri Ethics Commission data was not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 31 license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Wentzville's borders in OpenStreetMap (31 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Missouri yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 31 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Wentzville's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is recorded for some; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.

source.label: OpenStreetMap license-plate cameras (as mapped by DeFlock)

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Wentzville Police Department operates two DJI drones as of 2018, according to data compiled by the Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS003994, citing Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: As of April 2024, the Wentzville Police Department operates 25 Flock Safety automated license plate readers. The agency stores ALPR data for 30 days.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS013763, citing Flock Safety
